gen-fs-paquito-gf-lexend-zetta: Paquito is sturdy and warm, its lowercase filling the line almost like capitals. And Lexend Zetta drops in beneath it as a widely tracked sans of constant-width strokes, so the page moves from chunky serif to spaced-out ribbon.
gen-fs-paquito-gf-montserrat-alternates: Montserrat Alternates draws each letter like a thin steel rod bent into shape, with a wide-mouthed c. Then Paquito arrives as the sturdy serif above it, its lowercase packed full where the body stays slender.
gen-fs-pencerio-fs-sentient: Sentient reads with pinched, closed-in apertures and crossbars a touch finer than its stems, which gives it a sophisticated, contemporary hush. Pencerio, a formal calligraphic script with tightly fitted words, handles the flourish while Sentient handles the sustained reading.
gen-fs-plein-fs-literata: Plein greets the eye with open, approachable bowls. Its sans shapes look best big and brief, while Literata follows in bookish serif form, with stems a little heavier than their hairlines and curves that stay unclosed.
gen-fs-pramukh-rounded-gf-cascadia-mono: Cascadia Mono lines its letters up like pins in a wide board, a compact skyline where capitals blend into lowercase. But Pramukh Rounded above it is bunched tighter and friendlier, so a long stretch of text feels steady, like a rolling-ball pen.
gen-fs-pramukh-rounded-gf-lexend-exa: Lexend Exa reads clean and open, with a big x-height, stubby ascenders and descenders, and strokes that hold their width from stem to curve. Lexend Exa works nicely a step or two smaller than Pramukh Rounded, whose tight, friendly letters want the extra size.
gen-fs-pramukh-rounded-gf-lexend-giga: Friendly is the first word for Pramukh Rounded, its glyphs bunched close with open bowls like a tipped ladle. Lexend Giga is its opposite in spacing, flat single-weight lines with generous tracking, and that tight-versus-loose gap is what stands out.
gen-fs-pramukh-rounded-gf-lexend-mega: Lexend Mega looks drawn with one nib, its lowercase nearly as tall as the capitals. Over a longer passage it feels approachable and modern, with a visible gap in every c, while Pramukh Rounded above stays tight and bowl-shaped.
gen-fs-pramukh-rounded-gf-lexend-peta: Approachable and steady, Pramukh Rounded packs its glyphs tight with open bowls and large lowercase forms. Lexend Peta then follows with technical-pen curves that never thin, a wide-mouthed c and a big x-height, so the page feels cohesive yet distinct.
gen-fs-pramukh-rounded-gf-lexend-tera: Tight letters on top, wide-spaced marker strokes below, and a friendly feel throughout: Pramukh Rounded bunches its glyphs while Lexend Tera spreads out like stepping stones. Their spacing is the real difference.
